sentence: We will show that no matter how clever you are, no one‐player can face all 39 opponents in fewer than 39 rounds (since one plays exactly one match per round).

sentence: In fact the lower bound is 39 rounds (with the total number of distinct pairs being 780 and 20 new pairs per round, we have 780/20 = 39), and one may in fact “control” the outcomes so that every one of the 780 pairs occurs exactly once in 39 rounds.

sentence: ■ The setting

Immediately after the round the following happens:
 – On court 1, the loser (by rule) stays on court 1.

sentence: – On court 20, the winner stays on court 20.

sentence: – For every other court (and also for the “other half” of the players in courts 1 and 20), the winners move “to the right”: that is, if a player wins on court i (with i < 20) he goes to court i+1; and the losers (with i > 1) move “to the left” (the loser on court i with i > 1 goes to court i–1).
sentence-category-reason: Restates the movement rules for winners and losers on other courts.

sentence: Thus aside from the two boundary “exceptions” (loser on 1 and winner on 20), every match sends one player one step to the right and one step one step to the left.
